title: Battlegrounds History Data 1.1
description: An engine-neutral record of one Hearthstone Battlegrounds game: the states the game passed through and the actions that moved between them. SPECIFICATION.md holds the prose. Unknown members are allowed everywhere; a reader must ignore what it does not understand.

format.description: Fixed marker, so a reader can identify the file without guessing from its name.

version.description: The version of this specification the file claims to follow.

cardIdScheme.description: The naming system every cardId in this file comes from. 'hearthstone' means Blizzard's own text card ids, such as BG31_803.

players.description: Every seat the recorder knows about, in any order.

history.description: The game as an ordered list of entries. The order of the list is the order things happened.

specVersion.description: MAJOR.MINOR. A rise in MINOR only adds things. A rise in MAJOR may remove or redefine them.

ext.description: Anything a producer wants to keep that this format does not define. Key it by your own name, such as {"acme": {}}, so two producers cannot collide. No reader may depend on it.

identifier.description: A short name, unique inside this file.

openName.description: A vocabulary word this specification does not list. It must start with 'x-', so a reader can always tell a private word from a standard one.

cardId.description: The stable id of a card, in the file's cardIdScheme. This is the only field a reader may use to decide which card something is.

minionType.description: A minion type, which players also call a tribe. 'all' means the card counts as every type at once.

keyword.description: A printed ability that changes how a card fights or is bought.

cardType.description: What sort of card this is.

enchantment.description: Something attached to a card that changes it: a buff from a spell, a Dark Gift, a lasting effect.

card.description: One card as it stood at a moment: which card it is, and the numbers it showed.

entity.description: A name for this one physical copy, stable for as long as the copy exists. Two copies of the same card carry different entity names.

name.description: For display. Never match on it.

attack.description: Current attack, with every buff already added in.

health.description: Current health, with every buff already added in.

maxHealth.description: Health before damage, when the two differ.

tier.description: The tavern tier this card is sold at.

golden.description: A golden copy, made by collecting three of the same card.

cost.description: What it costs to buy or play at this moment.

costsHealth.description: The cost is paid in health rather than gold.

trinketTier.description: For a trinket only: which of the two trinket slots it fills. A lesser trinket is offered earlier in the game and a greater one later. A player holds at most one of each, and the two are chosen at different moments, so this is a property of the trinket and not a rarity.

playable.description: Whether the owner could legally buy or play it at this moment.

attached.description: Cards fused into this one, such as Mech parts added by magnetizing.

unknown.description: True when the recorder knows a card is here but cannot see which card it is. cardId is then absent.

ref.description: A pointer at one card in one place. Give an entity name, a position, or both. Positions count from 0, left to right.

player.description: Whose zone. Defaults to the acting player.

cardId.description: Repeats what the entity already says, but helps a file that carries no entity names.

zone.description: The contents of one zone, and an honest count of what the recorder could not see.

unknownCount.description: How many further cards sit in this zone whose identity the recorder cannot see.

frozen.description: Shop only: the shop is held over to the next turn.

recording.description: Facts about the file itself rather than about the game.

id.description: A name for this recording, unique to whoever produced it.

recorder.description: The program that produced the file.

kind.description: 'tracker' watches a live client. 'simulator' plays the game itself. 'replayParser' reads a stored game. 'manual' means a person typed it in.

truncated.description: The recording stops before the game did.

observer.description: Who was watching, and therefore what the file can be trusted to contain.

scope.description: 'lobby' means every seat was visible, which only a program that runs the whole game can claim. 'seat' means one player's point of view.

seat.description: The player whose point of view this is. Required when scope is 'seat'.

detail.description: How much the file contains, stated up front so a reader never has to read an absence as a fact.

combat.description: 'none': fights are not recorded at all. 'outcome': who won and what it cost. 'boards': also the two boards as they were sent in. 'events': also the blow by blow.

states.description: How often the file writes down a full picture of a seat.

entities.description: True when every card carries an entity name, so one copy can be followed through the whole game.

game.description: Facts about the lobby that hold for the whole game.

mode.description: 'solo' is eight players alone. 'duos' is four teams of two.

patch.description: The game build the recording came from, such as '34.2.0'.

minionTypes.description: The minion types this lobby drew. null means the recorder does not know.

anomaly.description: A lobby-wide rule change, when the season has them.

rng.description: Only a producer that generates its own randomness fills this in. It never replaces the recorded history.

id.description: How the rest of the file names this seat.

name.description: Display name. Leave it out if you would rather not publish it.

agent.description: The program that made this seat's decisions, when a person did not.

teammate.description: Duos only: the player sharing this team.

hero.description: The hero this seat played. Record it for every seat you learn it for, including opponents: the leaderboard shows an opponent's hero, so even a one-seat recording can fill this in.

heroPower.description: The ability printed on the hero. A one-seat recording usually knows only its own.

playerResult.description: How this seat finished. Every field is optional, because a one-seat recording may never learn some of them.

heroPowerUses.description: How many times this seat used its hero power all game.

trinkets.description: Trinkets this seat still held at the end.

board.description: The board this seat held when its game ended.

phase.description: 'recruit' is the shopping half of a turn. 'combat' is the fight that follows it.

seq.description: Position in the history. It rises strictly across the file. Gaps are allowed and mean nothing was recorded there.

note.description: A sentence for a person reading the file. Never authoritative.

actionEntry.description: Something a player chose to do.

accepted.description: False records an action the game refused. A refused action changes nothing.

actionData.description: The parts of an action. Which parts are required depends on the verb.

target.description: The single card the action was aimed at.

targets.description: Every card the action was aimed at, in the order the player picked them.

offer.description: The id of the offer event this choice answers.

option.description: Which option of that offer was taken, counted from 0.

mode.description: Which half of a Choose One card the player picked.

decision.description: Optional notes on how the choice was made. A program that ranks its options can say what it was choosing between. A person cannot, and leaves this out.

legalOptions.description: How many actions were legal at this moment.

probability.description: How likely the chooser was to pick this one.

value.description: The chooser's own score for the position.

considered.description: Other actions that were on the table.

refusals.description: Actions a rule removed before the chooser ever saw them. Anyone checking a suspect player needs the moves it was not allowed to make.

eventEntry.description: Something the game did, rather than something a player chose.

actor.description: The player the event happened to, when it concerns one seat.

eventData.description: The parts of an event. Which parts are required depends on the verb.

id.description: For an offer: the name a later 'choose' action points back at.

offerType.description: What sort of choice was put in front of the player.

options.description: The choices on the table, counted from 0.

hidden.description: True when the player had to commit before seeing the options. The options are then listed as unknown cards.

reason.description: Why this happened, when the game gives a reason.

cards.description: The cards this event concerns, such as a freshly dealt shop.

swing.description: Which swing of a multi-attack this is. Windfury gives two swings a turn, Mega-Windfury four.

attack.description: Change in attack, or the new value when 'absolute' is true.

health.description: Change in health, or the new value when 'absolute' is true.

absolute.description: The numbers are the new totals, not the change.

permanent.description: The change outlives the fight and travels back to the shop with the minion.

absorbed.description: A Divine Shield swallowed the damage, so the target lost no health.

poisonous.description: The damage destroys whatever it touches, however much health is left.

position.description: The board position a summoned minion appeared at, counted from 0.

times.description: How many times a trigger fired, when one entry stands for several firings.

upgradeCost.description: What the next tavern tier costs right now.

ghostOf.description: The fight is against a copy of a knocked-out player's board. Nothing that happens to the copy affects the player who once owned it.

combat.description: Ties every event of one fight together.

firstAttacker.description: The player whose board swings first.

winner.description: The winning player, or null for a draw.

healthAfter.description: null means the recorder could not see it.

board.description: The board sent into the fight, left to right.

hand.description: Only needed for the few cards whose combat text reads the owner's hand.

eliminated.description: This fight knocked the player out.

standing.description: One row of the leaderboard, which is all a player normally sees of the other seats.

hero.description: The hero this seat is playing. The leaderboard shows it, so a one-seat recording learns every opponent's hero even though it learns nothing else about them. Repeat it in players[].hero once you know it.

stateEntry.description: A full picture of one seat at one moment. Optional: a reader can also rebuild the state by replaying the entries.

actor.description: The seat this picture is of.

zones.description: Keyed by zone name: board, hand, shop, trinkets.

nextOpponent.description: The seat this player will fight next, announced before the recruit phase ends.

seatState.description: The numbers that describe a seat, apart from its cards.

tier.description: Tavern tier: how strong the cards in this seat's shop can be.

goldCap.description: The most gold this seat can be given at the start of a turn.

upgradeCost.description: What the next tavern tier costs right now. null at the top tier.
